message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
It includes:

1. **`gcloud` CLI** command – the easiest way if you already have the Cloud SDK installed.  
2. **REST API** request – useful if you want to embed the call in your own automation or use a language‑specific client library.  
3. **Prerequisites & notes** – what you need to have in place before you run the commands.

> ⚠️ **Important** – Replace the placeholder values (`YOUR_PROJECT_ID`, `YOUR_ZONE`, `YOUR_INSTANCE_NAME`) with your own data.

---

## 1. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# 1️⃣  Set your project and zone
export PROJECT_ID="YOUR_PROJECT_ID"
export ZONE="YOUR_ZONE"          # e.g., us-central1-a
export INSTANCE_NAME="YOUR_INSTANCE_NAME"

# 2️⃣  Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="n1-standard-8" \          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM (adjust as needed)
  --accelerator="type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1" \
  --image-family="ubuntu-2004-lts" \
  --image-project="ubuntu-os-cloud" \
  --boot-disk-size="100GB" \
  --boot-disk-type="pd-ssd" \
  --maintenance-policy="TERMINATE" \
  --restart-on-failure \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \   # optional: your custom script
  --tags=http-server,https-server \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration. `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs and 30 GB RAM. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the GPU. `nvidia-tesla-a6000` is the RTX A6000. |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Pulls the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image from the official Ubuntu Cloud image repository. |
| `--boot-disk-size` & `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk of 100 GB. |
| `--maintenance-policy` | `TERMINATE` means the VM will be stopped during maintenance events. |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Auto‑restarts if the VM crashes. |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional: run a shell script at first boot. |
| `--tags` | Network tags for firewall rules (e.g., allow HTTP/HTTPS). |
| `--scopes` | Grants the VM full Cloud Platform access. |

> **Tip:** If you need more GPUs or a different machine type, adjust the `--accelerator` and `--machine-type` flags accordingly.

---

## 2. Using the REST API (JSON)

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine API directly (e.g., from a script or a custom client), use the following POST request:

```http
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/YOUR_ZONE/instances
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "YOUR_INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "zones/YOUR_ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "zones/YOUR_ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/YOUR_ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  },
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y build-essential"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Steps to use the REST API

1. **Obtain an OAuth 2.0 access token** with the scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform`.  
   You can get one via `gcloud auth application-default print-access-token` or by using a service account key.  
2. Replace `YOUR_PROJECT_ID`, `YOUR_ZONE`, `YOUR_INSTANCE_NAME`, and `YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN` with your actual values.  
3. Send the request using `curl`, Postman, or any HTTP client library.

---

## 3. Prerequisites & Checklist

| Item | How to Verify / Setup |
|------|-----------------------|
| **Google Cloud SDK** | `gcloud version` – install from <https://cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/install> |
| **Compute Engine API enabled** | `gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com` |
| **Billing enabled** | Check in Cloud Console → Billing |
| **GPU quota** | `gcloud compute accelerator-types list --filter="zone:(YOUR_ZONE)"` – ensure you have quota for `nvidia-tesla-a6000` |
| **Service account** | If using REST, create a service account with `roles/compute.admin` and download its key. |
| **Firewall rules** | Ensure `http-server` and `https-server` tags are allowed in your VPC firewall. |
| **Region/Zone** | RTX A6000 GPUs are available in specific zones (e.g., `us-central1-a`, `us-east1-b`). Check availability: <https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/gpus#available_zones> |

---

## 4. Quick One‑liner (for automation scripts)

```bash
gcloud compute instances create YOUR_INSTANCE_NAME \
  --project=YOUR_PROJECT_ID \
  --zone=YOUR_ZONE \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh
```

Just copy‑paste the line above into your terminal (after replacing placeholders) and hit **Enter**.

---

### Final Notes

* **Cost** – RTX A6000 GPUs are expensive. Monitor your billing dashboard closely.  
* **GPU drivers** – The Ubuntu 20.04 image comes with the NVIDIA driver pre‑installed, but you may want to install the latest CUDA toolkit or other libraries after the instance boots.  
* **Shutdown** – Remember to stop or delete the instance when you’re done to avoid incurring charges.

Happy GPU computing! 🚀
